question.text: A trader holds a long position of 50 lots in USDINR futures. Entry price: Rs. 83.20. Day 1 DSP: Rs. 83.50. Day 2 DSP: Rs. 82.90. What is the cumulative MTM after Day 2?

explanation.text: The Logic: Daily MTM uses the daily settlement price and open positions are carried forward at the latest settlement price. Cumulative MTM = 50 x 1000 x (82.90 - 83.20) = 50,000 x (-0.30) = -Rs. 15,000. Day by day: Day 1 = +Rs. 15,000 (long, settled at 83.50), Day 2 = -Rs. 30,000 (carried at 83.50, settled at 82.90), net = -Rs. 15,000. The Trap: The cumulative P&L always equals (current DSP - entry price) x quantity, irrespective of the intermediate MTM path; adding the daily figures incorrectly can suggest a larger loss. Note: Daily MTM settlement ensures losses are collected each day, which is a core clearing-side risk-management control against default.
